assignments.title: Primary Source Report: Locke and Montesquieu
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
Locke and Montesquieu
The Enlightenment
16 points · text entry
✦ ✧ ✦
Before you start

Finish both lessons and read both sources first. Your notes from each page are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the page, so open it before you write. Then write your answers and submit them in this assignment.

QUESTIONS
1. John Locke published his Second Treatise in 1689. Montesquieu published The Spirit of the Laws in 1748. For each writer, say what danger in government he is most worried about and what remedy he offers. Quote a few words from each passage to support your answer.
2. Choose one sentence or phrase from Locke's passage. Quote it in a few words, then explain in your own words what it claims about where a government's right to rule comes from, and what the people may do if a ruler breaks that trust.
3. Locke and Montesquieu both want to limit government, but they do not rely on the same safeguard. Using evidence from both passages, explain how the two safeguards differ. Then say whether each one needs something the other does not, such as an active people or separate branches of government.
4. Montesquieu wrote about England as a visitor who studied its government, and the lesson “Locke, Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau, and Smith” says his picture was a little too neat. Why should a historian be careful before treating his account as a plain report of how England was governed? Name one other kind of evidence that could test it.
GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)
Criteria Excellent (4) Proficient (3) Developing (2) Beginning (1)
Understanding of the material
4 pts		 Reads both sources accurately and draws on specific details from each, along with what the week's lessons taught. Reads both sources accurately but uses few specific details, or leans on only one. Shows partial understanding of one or both sources, with some errors or vague claims. Misreads the sources or does not refer to them.
Quality of reasoning
4 pts		 Connects each claim to evidence and compares the sources with care. Explains how the two remedies differ and what each one assumes. Supports most claims with evidence. The comparison is sound but not fully developed. States conclusions with little support, or describes the sources without comparing them. Offers opinions without evidence from the sources.
Clarity and precision of expression
4 pts		 Writes in clear, well-organized sentences. Quotations are short, accurate, and introduced. Writing is clear with minor lapses in organization or precision. Writing is often unclear or disorganized, and quotations are unclear or misplaced. Writing is too unclear to follow.
Intellectual honesty
4 pts		 Names the limits of what each source can show and says what remains uncertain without overclaiming. Acknowledges at least one limit of the evidence. Mentions limits only in passing, or claims more than the sources allow. Treats each source as complete and beyond question.
Total:
16 pts total
SUBMISSION

Answer all four questions in complete sentences. Submit your answers in the text box on the Canvas assignment page. Aim for one solid paragraph for each question. You do not need an outside source. Your teacher will read your work and return a rubric score with a short comment.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: The Enlightenment
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
The Enlightenment
2 questions · survey · one attempt
✦ ✧ ✦
Essential question for this week
What did Enlightenment thinkers believe protects liberty, and how did their answers differ?
Instructions

Welcome to The Enlightenment. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

From Newton to the Salons

  • Explain how Newton's work changed the way educated Europeans thought about nature and knowledge.
  • Describe how books, coffeehouses, and salons spread new ideas.
  • Recognize the limits and dangers the Enlightenment faced.

Locke, Montesquieu, Voltaire, Rousseau, and Smith

  • Summarize the central argument of each of the five thinkers.
  • Compare the claims that government rests on consent and that it must be limited by checks.
  • Explain how each thinker's ideas connect to the problems of liberty and order.

discussions.title: Discussion: What Protects Liberty: Consent or Checks?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
What Protects Liberty: Consent or Checks?
The Enlightenment
10 points · threaded discussion
✦ ✧ ✦
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

Locke taught that a government rules by the consent of the governed, and that people may resist a ruler who attacks their rights. Montesquieu feared that anyone who holds power is tempted to abuse it, and he wanted power divided so that one part could check another. Rousseau also rested government on consent, but he placed it in the whole community.

Take a position. Which does more to protect liberty: the consent of the governed or checks on those who govern? Support your position with at least two specific details from the lessons, and include one detail that points the other way. Explain why you weigh the evidence as you do.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Takes a clear position, supports it with at least two specific details from the lessons, and deals fairly with a detail that points the other way. Takes a position but gives only one detail, or stays general, or ignores the opposing detail. No post, or no clear position.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
